11	def can_be_chunked(attributes: Dict[str, Any]) -> bool:
12	    """Return whether a rolling window can safely be computed chunk by chunk.
13	
14	    Each chunk is extended on its left by ``window`` items, so its own items are
15	    computed with the exact same data as in the sequential case. This trick only works
16	    if:
17	
18	    - the window is expressed as a fixed number of items (an offset based window, like
19	      ``"2s"``, would need a time based left extension),
20	    - the window is not centered (a centered window also needs data on its right),
21	    - the window is not strided (``step``), since strides are computed from the
22	      beginning of the data.
23	
24	    When one of these conditions is not met, the computation is delegated to a single
25	    worker, so the result stays correct.
26	    """
27	    if attributes.get("center", False):
28	        return False
29	
30	    if attributes.get("step", None) not in (None, 1):
31	        return False
32	
33	    window = attributes.get("window", None)
34	
35	    return isinstance(window, int) and not isinstance(window, bool)
36

38	class ExpandingChunk:
39	    """A chunk of an expanding window computation.
40	
41	    ``values`` contains every item from the beginning of the data up to the end of the
42	    chunk, and ``start`` is the position of the first item which really belongs to this
43	    chunk.
44	    """
45	
46	    __slots__ = ("values", "start")
47	
48	    def __init__(self, values: Union[pd.Series, pd.DataFrame], start: int) -> None:
49	        self.values = values
50	        self.start = start
51	
52	    def __len__(self) -> int:
53	        # The number of times the user defined function is called for this chunk.
54	        return len(self.values)
55

58	    class Apply(DataType):
59	        @staticmethod
60	        def get_chunks(
61	            nb_workers: int, rolling: Rolling, **kwargs
62	        ) -> Iterator[pd.Series]:
63	            attributes = get_window_attributes(rolling)
64	
65	            if not can_be_chunked(attributes):
66	                yield rolling.obj
67	                return
68	
69	            chunks = chunk(len(rolling.obj), nb_workers, attributes["window"])
70	
71	            for chunk_ in chunks:
72	                yield rolling.obj.iloc[chunk_]
73	
74	        @staticmethod
75	        def get_work_extra(data: Rolling) -> Dict[str, Any]:
76	            return {"attributes": get_window_attributes(data)}
77	
78	        @staticmethod
79	        def work(
80	            data: pd.Series,
81	            user_defined_function: Callable,
82	            user_defined_function_args: tuple,
83	            user_defined_function_kwargs: Dict[str, Any],
84	            extra: Dict[str, Any],
85	        ) -> pd.Series:
86	            attributes: Dict[str, Any] = extra["attributes"]
87	            worker_index: int = extra["worker_index"]
88	
89	            result = data.rolling(**attributes).apply(
90	                user_defined_function,
91	                *user_defined_function_args,
92	                **user_defined_function_kwargs,
93	            )
94	
95	            if worker_index == 0 or not can_be_chunked(attributes):
96	                return result
97	
98	            # This chunk has been extended on its left by `window` items, so the rolling
99	            # computation is correct even for its own first items. These extra items
100	            # belong to the previous chunk: remove them from the result.
101	            return result.iloc[attributes["window"] :]
102	
103	        @staticmethod
104	        def reduce(datas: Iterable[pd.Series], extra: Dict[str, Any]) -> pd.Series:
105	            return pd.concat(datas, copy=False)

108	class SeriesExpanding:
109	    """Parallelization of ``Series.expanding().apply(...)``.
110	
111	    An expanding window always starts at the first item of the data, so a chunk cannot
112	    be computed independently from the chunks before it. Each worker therefore receives
113	    every item from the beginning of the data up to the end of its own chunk, and only
114	    returns the part of the result which belongs to its own chunk.
115	    """
116	
117	    class Apply(DataType):
118	        @staticmethod
119	        def get_chunks(
120	            nb_workers: int, expanding: Expanding, **kwargs
121	        ) -> Iterator[ExpandingChunk]:
122	            for chunk_ in chunk(len(expanding.obj), nb_workers):
123	                yield ExpandingChunk(
124	                    expanding.obj.iloc[slice(0, chunk_.stop)], chunk_.start or 0
125	                )
126	
127	        @staticmethod
128	        def get_work_extra(data: Expanding) -> Dict[str, Any]:
129	            return {"attributes": get_window_attributes(data)}
130	
131	        @staticmethod
132	        def work(
133	            data: ExpandingChunk,
134	            user_defined_function: Callable,
135	            user_defined_function_args: tuple,
136	            user_defined_function_kwargs: Dict[str, Any],
137	            extra: Dict[str, Any],
138	        ) -> pd.Series:
139	            attributes: Dict[str, Any] = extra["attributes"]
140	
141	            result = data.values.expanding(**attributes).apply(
142	                user_defined_function,
143	                *user_defined_function_args,
144	                **user_defined_function_kwargs,
145	            )
146	
147	            return result.iloc[data.start :]
148	
149	        @staticmethod
150	        def reduce(datas: Iterable[pd.Series], extra: Dict[str, Any]) -> pd.Series:
151	            return pd.concat(datas, copy=False)

10	def chunk(nb_item: int, nb_chunks: int, start_offset=0) -> List[slice]:
11	    """
12	    Return `nb_chunks` slices of approximatively `nb_item / nb_chunks` each.
13	
14	    Parameters
15	    ----------
16	    nb_item : int
17	        Total number of items
18	
19	    nb_chunks : int
20	        Number of chunks to return
21	
22	    start_offset : int
23	        Shift start of slice by this amount
24	
25	    Returns
26	    -------
27	    A list of slices
28	
29	    Examples
30	    --------
31	    >>> chunks = chunk(103, 4)
32	    >>> chunks
33	    [slice(0, 26, None), slice(26, 52, None), slice(52, 78, None), slice(78, 103, None)]
34	    """
35	    if nb_item == 0:
36	        # Nothing to compute, but at least one (empty) chunk has to be returned so
37	        # workers are able to return an empty result with the correct type.
38	        return [slice(0)]
39	
40	    if nb_chunks <= 0:
41	        raise ValueError(
42	            f"nb_chunks should be a strictly positive integer, got {nb_chunks}"
43	        )
44	
45	    if nb_item <= nb_chunks:
46	        return [slice(max(0, idx - start_offset), idx + 1) for idx in range(nb_item)]
47	
48	    quotient = nb_item // nb_chunks
49	    remainder = nb_item % nb_chunks
50	
51	    quotients = [quotient] * nb_chunks
52	    remainders = [1] * remainder + [0] * (nb_chunks - remainder)
53	
54	    nb_elems_per_chunk = [
55	        quotient + remainder for quotient, remainder in zip(quotients, remainders)
56	    ]
57	
58	    accumulated = list(itertools.accumulate(nb_elems_per_chunk))
59	    shifted_accumulated = accumulated.copy()
60	    shifted_accumulated.insert(0, 0)
61	    shifted_accumulated.pop()
62	
63	    return [
64	        slice(max(0, begin - start_offset), end)
65	        for begin, end in zip(shifted_accumulated, accumulated)
66	    ]

146	    }

156	def get_groupby_window_groups(window: Any) -> List[Tuple[Any, Any, Index]]:
157	    """
158	    Split the data of a ``RollingGroupby`` / ``ExpandingGroupby`` into its groups, the
159	    exact same way pandas does it internally.
160	
161	    Parameters
162	    ----------
163	    window: A pandas ``RollingGroupby`` or ``ExpandingGroupby`` object.
164	
165	    Returns
166	    -------
167	    A list of ``(group_key, group_data, group_index)`` tuples, in the same order as the
168	    rows of the result computed by pandas.
169	
170	    ``group_data`` is indexed the way pandas indexes the windows it gives to the user
171	    defined function, and ``group_index`` is the real index of the group, used to build
172	    the index of the result.
173	
174	    Notes
175	    -----
176	    pandas computes the windows on the object reordered by group
177	    (``BaseWindowGroupby._create_data``), but pairs those reordered values with the
178	    **original** (not reordered) index (``BaseWindow._on``). The index a user defined
179	    function sees is therefore the original index taken at the position of the item in
180	    the reordered object. This has to be reproduced exactly, otherwise a user defined
181	    function which uses the index of its window (with ``raw=False``) would not return
182	    the same result as pandas.
183	    """
184	    obj = window.obj
185	    indices = window._grouper.indices
186	
187	    if len(obj) == 0 or not indices:
188	        return []
189	
190	    order = np.concatenate(list(indices.values())).astype(np.int64)
191	
192	    positions_in_reordered_object = np.empty(len(obj), dtype=np.int64)
193	    positions_in_reordered_object[order] = np.arange(len(order), dtype=np.int64)
194	
195	    groups = []
196	
197	    for key, positions in indices.items():
198	        positions = np.asarray(positions, dtype=np.int64)
199	        group_data = obj.take(positions)
200	        group_index = group_data.index
201	        group_data.index = obj.index.take(positions_in_reordered_object[positions])
202	
203	        groups.append((key, group_data, group_index))
204	
205	    return groups

210	    Build the index of the result of a window computation on a single group: the group
211	    key(s), followed by the original index of the group.
212	    """
213	    keys = key if isinstance(key, tuple) else (key,)
214	    nb_items = len(group_index)
215	
216	    arrays: List[Any] = [[key_item] * nb_items for key_item in keys]
217	
218	    if isinstance(group_index, pd.MultiIndex):

221	            for level in range(group_index.nlevels)

import numpy as np, pandas as pd
from pandarallel import pandarallel

def f(x):
    return (x.multiply(pd.Series(range(1, len(x)+1), dtype="float"))).sum()

for pb in (False, True):
    pandarallel.initialize(progress_bar=pb, use_memory_fs=None, nb_workers=2, verbose=0)

        df = pd.DataFrame(dict(a=np.random.randint(1,8,size), b=list(range(size))))
        res = df.b.rolling(4).apply(f, raw=False)
        par = df.b.rolling(4).parallel_apply(f, raw=False)
        print("graded-style series.rolling(4) nb_workers=2 size", size, "pb", pb, "equals:", res.equals(par), len(res), len(par))
EOF

from pandarallel.utils import chunk
for (n,w,win) in [(5,2,4),(1000,4,400),(1000,2,4),(1,2,4),(5,8,4),(20,8,4),(1000,2,600),(12,4,4),(9,4,4)]:
    sl = chunk(n,w,win)
    # simulate: worker i keeps result.iloc[win:] for i>0
    kept = []
    for i, s in enumerate(sl):
        idxs = list(range(n))[s]
        kept += idxs if i == 0 else idxs[win:]
    ok = kept == list(range(n))
    print(f"n={n} workers={w} window={win} slices={sl} kept={len(kept)}/{n} correct={ok} missing={sorted(set(range(n))-set(kept))[:12]}")
EOF

import numpy as np, pandas as pd
from pandarallel import pandarallel

pandarallel.initialize(nb_workers=4, progress_bar=False, use_memory_fs=None, verbose=0)
s = pd.Series(np.arange(1000, dtype=float))
seq = s.rolling(400).apply(np.sum, raw=True)
par = s.rolling(400).parallel_apply(np.sum, raw=True)
print("n=1000 w=400 workers=4 -> len seq/par:", len(seq), len(par), "missing:", list(seq.index.difference(par.index))[:5], "...", list(seq.index.difference(par.index))[-3:])
print("  non-NaN seq/par:", seq.notna().sum(), par.notna().sum())

# DataFrame.rolling
df = pd.DataFrame(np.arange(15, dtype=float).reshape(5,3), columns=list("abc"))
pandarallel.initialize(nb_workers=2, progress_bar=False, use_memory_fs=None, verbose=0)
print("df.rolling(4) shapes:", df.rolling(4).apply(np.sum, raw=True).shape, df.rolling(4).parallel_apply(np.sum, raw=True).shape)

# default nb_workers (cpu_count) with a moderate window on 1000 rows
pandarallel.initialize(progress_bar=False, use_memory_fs=None, verbose=0)
s = pd.Series(np.arange(1000, dtype=float))
for w in (4, 16, 20, 50):
    a = s.rolling(w).apply(np.sum, raw=True); b = s.rolling(w).parallel_apply(np.sum, raw=True)
    print(f"default workers, window={w}: equals={a.equals(b)} len {len(a)}->{len(b)} missing={list(a.index.difference(b.index))[:8]}")

# groupby rolling / expanding graded paths, nb_workers=2
pandarallel.initialize(progress_bar=False, use_memory_fs=None, nb_workers=2, verbose=0)
def f(x): return (x.multiply(pd.Series(range(1, len(x)+1), dtype="float"))).sum()
for size in (1000, 1):
    df = pd.DataFrame(dict(a=np.random.randint(1,8,size), b=list(range(size))))
    r1 = df.groupby("a").b.rolling(4).apply(f, raw=False)
    r2 = df.groupby("a").b.rolling(4).parallel_apply(f, raw=False)
    e1 = df.groupby("a").b.expanding().apply(f, raw=False)
    e2 = df.groupby("a").b.expanding().parallel_apply(f, raw=False)
    s1 = df.b.expanding().apply(f, raw=False); s2 = df.b.expanding().parallel_apply(f, raw=False)
    print("size", size, "groupby-rolling equals:", r1.equals(r2), "groupby-expanding:", e1.equals(e2), "series-expanding:", s1.equals(s2))
EOF
